terms.definition: The order of the planets by distance from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
terms.function: Sets the timeline road's structure — every stop follows this order, and every orbit/trivia fact follows the order too.
terms.whereItIs: The sequence of planet spheres standing on the road.
terms.whyItMatters: Distance order is the default mental axis of the whole solar system: planets, missions, images, and temperatures all follow it.

terms.definition: The average Sun–Earth distance, about 150 million km — the ruler this timeline is drawn in.
terms.function: Lets the whole road use one readable scale, from 0 at the Sun to 30 at Neptune.
terms.whereItIs: The thin ruler band floating the length of the road.
terms.whyItMatters: Without the AU, distances collapse into unreadable numbers — with it, every step reads in understandable multiples.

terms.definition: How long sunlight takes to reach each planet's position along the road.
terms.function: Turns the ruler into a clock: about 3 minutes to Mercury, 8 to Earth, 43 to Jupiter, and over 4 hours to Neptune.
terms.whereItIs: The traveling light counter panel that moves along the ruler when played.
terms.whyItMatters: Light time is the human feel for cosmic distance — minutes along this road become years between the stars.

terms.definition: The band of rocky leftovers orbiting between Mars and Jupiter, marking the inner/outer divide.
terms.function: Splits the road into two neighborhoods: inside the belt the compact inner planets, outside it the distant giants.
terms.whereItIs: The scattered crowd of tiny stone spheres across the road in the belt zone.
terms.whyItMatters: The belt sits in the widest empty stretch of the road — the solar system's biggest boundary.

terms.definition: The two halves of the timeline separated by the asteroid belt: the inner rocky worlds (Mercury–Mars) and the outer giants (Jupiter–Neptune).
terms.function: Groups the planets into families that share size, composition, and spacing.
terms.whereItIs: Both halves of the road, divided at the belt band.
terms.whyItMatters: Four planets in the first 1.5 AU, four more across the next 28.5 AU — the timeline itself tells the story.
